title: Effects of a thermoplastic foot orthosis on patellofemoral pain in a collegiate athlete: a single-subject design.
journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: To evaluate the effects of a foot orthosis on pain and function by controlling forefoot pronation.

sections.label: BACKGROUND
sections.text: Foot orthoses have been recommended to treat patellofemoral pain by controlling excessive pronation, but few studies have used an experimental design to validate this approach.

sections.label: METHODS AND MEASURES
sections.text: A 19-year-old collegiate softball player had an acute onset of patellofemoral pain in her left knee. A visual analog scale was used to assess pain intensity and a functional index questionnaire (FIQ) was used to measure the subject's perceived functional level.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: Statistical analysis using the celeration line technique showed significant improvements between all the consecutive baseline and intervention phases of the VAS data and in 7 of the 9 paired phases of the FIQ data.

sections.label: CONCLUSIONS
sections.text: Limiting pronation with a thermoplastic orthosis was an effective treatment for this subject.
